$comment: Central configuration. Every generator/validator reads this file. Override any value with the matching YUHANA_* environment variable (see src/config.py).

site.$comment_viewer_region: Where the TV actually is. This is an assumption - inferred from the project being built around Bangladesh priority and the owner's original playlist - and it is here rather than in code so it can be corrected in one place. It matters because validation runs on a GitHub runner in the United States: a South Asian channel fenced to its home region refuses the runner and serves the owner. Those channels are published on the strength of where the viewer is, not where the probe is.

ssiptv.$comment: Limits taken from SS IPTV operator documentation and Smart-TV memory constraints.
ssiptv.$comment_navigation: Sports and Kids stay as one alphabetical list each: the owner asked to browse them straight through, and pagination already keeps any single screen inside the tile budget.
ssiptv.$comment_subsplit: never_subsplit no longer means never: those categories stay on one flat screen while they fit inside protected_subsplit_threshold, and split by country beyond it. Against the full iptv-org index Sports and Kids run to four figures, and a flat list cut into a dozen numbered pages is harder to navigate than a country folder. Bangladesh is still never split - it is a country bucket already.
ssiptv.$comment_doors: Every channel is reachable by country, by genre and by first letter. One hierarchy cannot serve eight thousand channels - genre-first made the owner guess whether Zee Bangla was Entertainment, General or Movies, and a wrong guess meant starting over. Three doors mean a wrong guess costs a click. min_country_folder is the smallest country that earns its own screen; anything smaller joins the single Others folder at the end.
ssiptv.$comment_pinned: Kept at the top of the By Country screen, above the continents. These are the countries the owner actually watches; everything else is one press further in.

health_gate.$comment: Refuses to publish a validation run that looks like a vantage-point failure rather than a real outage. Only active once a baseline of previously-ACTIVE channels exists.

validation.$comment_reliability: Default 0.5: a channel that is up more often than not earns a tile. Bangladesh gets more latitude at 0.25 because it is the priority market and validation runs from a US datacentre, which inflates failure rates for BD-hosted streams; Green TV, Desh TV, Global TV and Channel S were all being withheld on distance rather than on being broken.
validation.$comment_slow_degraded: DEGRADED covers three unrelated conditions: a slow origin (plays, just starts slower), an unfetchable segment or variant (black screen), and the holding state for a channel that failed once but not enough times to be condemned. Publishing only ACTIVE conflated them and dropped T Sports HD from the Bangladesh screen on 38 of 46 successful probes. A channel is re-admitted only when the recorded reason is latency, consecutive_failures is 0, and reliability is at least slow_degraded_min_reliability.
validation.$comment_region_blocked: No channel is excluded for where it is - the owner's explicit instruction. A refusal (403/451) or a source geo tag is published wherever the channel is, not only inside the viewer's region. The previous rule re-admitted South Asian channels only, on the reasoning that a US channel refusing a US probe would refuse Dhaka too. That reasoning is a guess about somebody else's CDN, and a guess is not a measurement. The owner's TV is the only instrument that can settle it.
validation.$comment_concurrency: Raised from 8 for the full iptv-org catalogue - roughly 10,000 channels instead of 1,800. per_host_concurrency and per_host_delay_seconds are unchanged, so no single origin is probed any harder than before; only the number of DIFFERENT hosts in flight goes up.
validation.$comment_check_budget: 40 minutes. The full aggregator index does not fit in one CI run, so a run probes never-checked channels first, then the least recently verified, and stops at the first chunk boundary past the budget. The next run continues where it stopped, so the whole catalogue is covered over a few passes and no channel is starved. Chunked rather than cancelled mid-probe: an interrupted probe would count as a failure and push a working channel towards OFFLINE on nothing but a clock.
validation.$comment_tls: Verification is always tried first. Only a certificate-verification failure - the host answered, its chain is untrusted - is retried without verification, and the channel is flagged tls_unverified. This is consistency, not indifference: the playlist already carries 902 plain-http streams with no certificate and no encryption at all, and the owner's own working playlist was 31% http. Holding https streams to a standard the rest of the list is not held to withheld 195 channels for nothing. These streams carry no credentials, because a URL that does is excluded outright.
validation.$comment_candidates: A dead URL is not a dead channel: an operator rotates a path and the aggregator is slow to notice. data/candidates.json lists alternatives for a condemned channel, each probed with the same validation as anything else and adopted only if it passes. Capped, because this is a handful of plausible endpoints for a free-to-air channel on hosts already in use, not a scan.
validation.$comment_blackscreen: Two causes of a black screen that every earlier check passed. First, the segment probe accepted any non-empty body with a 200, so an origin answering every path with an HTML error page or a 'stream offline' placeholder was reported ACTIVE; the bytes must now look like MPEG-TS, fMP4 or ADTS. Second, a dead encoder behind a live CDN serves a playlist whose window never moves - everything fetches and the player buffers forever - so a live playlist is re-read after live_edge_wait_seconds and must have advanced. The re-read costs a few seconds per channel, so it is spent on the categories and sources in deep_check_*, where the owner actually watches. The segment-content check is free and applies to all.
validation.$comment_failures: 2, not 3. Scheduled runs land every 4 to 11 hours in practice rather than the 3 the cron asks for, so three strikes left a dead channel on the TV for up to 36 hours. Two brings that to roughly 24 at worst, and the candidate-URL retry plus the reliability floor already guard against one bad probe condemning a good channel.
validation.$comment_decode: ffmpeg decodes a few seconds of the stream and reports frames and black time. It is the only check that says a television will show something: a container with no video stream, and one whose every frame is black, both pass every outside check and play as a black screen. pix_th is 0.10 and the black threshold 0.95, so a dark scene in a film is not mistaken for a dead feed. Scope is bounded: the owner's own categories and sources every run, plus decode_rotation_per_run channels whose video has never been confirmed, oldest first, so that backlog clears over days rather than never. When ffmpeg is absent nothing is withheld on its account.
validation.$comment_decode_budget: Decoding runs inside the ordinary probe, so it spends the same 40-minute budget. At 30s worst case per channel and 40 in flight, the owner's own set plus 400 rotation channels costs at most about eight minutes of that budget and usually far less. The backlog of channels never decoded clears in roughly three days of normal runs.
validation.$comment_proven: OFF everywhere by default (0 disables it), ON for Bangladesh. A Bangladeshi channel that has answered at least 2 probes keeps its tile through a DEGRADED with no definitive fault recorded, and through up to 8 consecutive non-definitive failures. Me TV at 96 of 98 probes, Ekushey TV at 67 of 68 and Green TV twice over were all pulled while sitting in DEGRADED with nothing definitive against them. Scoped to one market on purpose. Every reading of a Bangladeshi origin here is taken from a US datacentre, so the noise floor for this market is far higher than the rest, and a gate tuned on global data has now misfired on it three times running. Relaxing the whole catalogue to fix one region would be the wrong trade; a channel that has never worked gets nothing from this anywhere.
validation.$comment_definitive_grace: Consecutive definitive failures - a 404, a body that is not a manifest, an unfetchable segment - allowed before the tile goes. One everywhere else: a 404 is a 404. Two for Bangladesh, because a single bad reading against a long record of good ones is more likely a moment than a death, and every reading of a Bangladeshi origin is taken from the wrong continent. A channel that has never once worked gets no grace.

security.$comment_https: OFF, and it should stay off. This was switched on assuming SS IPTV refuses plain-http streams as mixed content. That assumption was never tested and was wrong: the owner's original working playlist was 31% plain http and played fine. The gate removed 333 channels including AXN, Star Movies, HBO, Sony Max and Star Sports. The other gates here are evidence-based; this one was not.
security.$comment_denied_hosts: General-purpose shorteners only. These can point anywhere, they are not operated by anyone in the streaming chain, and their target changes without notice. jmp2.uk and the Pluto stitcher hosts used to be on this list: that was a blanket ban standing in for a check we were not making, and it withheld 1,020 channels that probe ACTIVE at 92% reliability. The publication gate now runs its safety rules on the recorded redirect destination as well as the advertised URL, which is the real answer.

policy.$comment: Content-rights gating. 'require_rights_review' blocks a source from the published playlist until a human sets redistribution_allowed.

movies.$comment: Movie library tuning. min_rating_top_rated gates the Top Rated collection; min_playable_bytes rejects a 'movie' that is really an error page or a trailer.
movies.$comment_min_rating_publish: Withhold a film whose IMDb rating is BELOW this. A film with no rating is kept: not knowing is not the same as knowing it is bad. Set to 0 to disable.
movies.$comment_runtime: A movie library must hold movies. Archive collections are full of ephemeral shorts, talks and test footage; 60 minutes is the feature threshold and an unknown runtime cannot be confirmed as a feature.

ingest.$comment_retention: Circuit breaker for the ingest step, the counterpart to validation's health gate. save_channels replaces the registry, so one source failing to download would delete every channel it carries - and with the full aggregator index that is most of the catalogue. An ingest that returns less than this fraction of what is already on disk is refused, the registry is left untouched and the run fails loudly.
ingest.$comment_orphans: A channel removed from its source list is kept and keeps being probed. Aggregator lists churn, and a curator dropping an entry they could not reach is not a verdict on whether it plays in Dhaka. A channel still answering is kept indefinitely; one that has stopped is kept for this many days from its last successful verification, so it has a real chance to come back before it is let go.
